0.label: Event happened
0.notes: Base flag, always set on every real event.

1.label: Unresolved
1.notes: Doesn't reliably track event type, visual motion, or audio — the same real-world event has produced different bit 1 values on two different camera instances filming the same thing. Points to something per-camera/instance (sensitivity, firmware, internal bucketing) rather than anything about the event itself. Modifier bit, never shown as a filter category.

8.label: Motion detected
8.notes: Set when a fresh companion type=5 "Motion detected" eventlog entry lands in this exact 5-second bucket. Not a general motion-magnitude signal — an AI class (Person/Vehicle/Pet) can fire a genuinely new detection without this bit being set.

10.label: Tampering detected
10.notes: Revised from an earlier wrong guess of "QR Code".

12.label: Digital input (active)
12.notes: Only the active direction has been triggered so far; inactive is unconfirmed.

24.label: Face Detect
24.notes: Proposed as a plausible 4th member of the Person/Vehicle/Pet class-bit family. Not yet observed on any camera.

24.label: Defocus Detection
24.notes: Fits the top of the sequential Smart Event menu-order pattern (see bits 25-31) exactly, but never directly triggered or eventlog-cross-referenced.

25.label: Scene Change Detection
25.notes: Flag 33554435 is eventlog-confirmed as Scene Change Detection on a Hikvision camera and as Person Detect on the Reolink — a direct brand collision.

26.label: Face Detection
26.notes: Seen once on a Hikvision camera with only Face recognition enabled, no vehicle involved, and its position matches the sequential menu-order pattern exactly (between Scene Change Detection and Intrusion Detection). A likely third brand collision, not yet independently confirmed the way bits 25/27 are.

27.label: Intrusion Detection
27.notes: Confirmed brand collision, independently twice: flag 134217731 and again on 134217729.

31.label: Unattended Baggage Detection
31.notes: Sign bit — flag prints negative in the app since event_map's flag is a signed 32-bit field.

reserved:0.label: Object Removal Detection
reserved:0.notes: The 32-bit flag budget is fully spoken for, so this detection type is signaled through the previously-always-0 reserved RLE field instead. Only ever observed as 0 or 1 so far.
